problem: Modular ObjectNav methods such as SemExp fail mostly because of poor long-term goal selection ('where to go'), and RL policies trained on semantic maps generalize poorly to unseen scenes.
motivation: Modular RL improves sample efficiency and sim-to-real transfer over end-to-end RL, but goal selection from a semantic map remains the bottleneck. DrQ showed that image augmentation plus Q-function regularization improves RL from pixels, so the authors apply the same idea to semantic maps.
key_idea: Replace SemExp's PPO goal policy with a DrQ-style off-policy actor-critic that uses a conv encoder on the semantic map, random-shift augmentation and augmented Q-target/Q-value averaging to pick long-term goals.
insight: Augmentation choice matters: in the augmentation comparison (Table 3), random shift (SR 0.637) beats flip (0.597), grayscale (0.596) and rotate (0.604). There is no ablation removing the encoder, the regularization or the actor-critic, so the sources of the gain over SemExp are not isolated. Gains are also measured with tiny training (10 scenes, 1M frames).
method: Semantic Mapping: SemExp-style pipeline using Mask R-CNN, depth point clouds and pose to build a (C+2)xMxM top-down map with obstacle, explored and per-category channels (5cm cells)
Encoder Network: 4 conv layers (3x3, 32 channels, stride 1) + FC + LayerNorm + tanh giving 50-d features from the map, position history and goal category
Actor-Critic: SAC-style actor and clipped double-Q critic (3-layer MLPs, hidden dim 1024); the encoder is updated only by critic gradients; long-term goal sampled every 25 steps
Data augmentation: random shift (pad 4, random crop) on semantic maps; flip, grayscale and rotate were also tried
Q-function regularization: DrQ-style averaging of target Q over K=2 and of Q over M=2 augmentations
Local Policy: Fast Marching Method planner on the obstacle channel to reach the long-term goal; reward is the decrease in distance to the nearest target instance

setting.backbone: CNN encoder + actor-critic MLPs (trained from scratch, DrQ/SAC style); Mask R-CNN (pretrained) for segmentation
setting.training_data: 10 randomly sampled Gibson Tiny train scenes per run, 1M frames, repeated 5 times
setting.observation: RGB-D 640x480 + odometry (x, y, theta) + target category
setting.action_space: High-level long-term goal on the map, executed by FMM planner into low-level Habitat actions (move_forward, turn left/right, stop)
setting.privileged: none (pose from odometry; no GT map)

numbers.eval_set_note: Gibson Tiny val, 5 scenes, 200 episodes per scene (1000 episodes), 6 object categories; models trained on only 10 train scenes for 1M frames
numbers.extra: Trained on 10 scenes x 1M frames; 6 categories; 500 step limit; 1m success radius

numbers_note: Success and SPL are printed as fractions (0.637), not percentages. Table 2 gives per-split results (average Success 0.629, SPL 0.305, DTS 1.654). Table 3 gives the augmentation ablation.
results: On Gibson Tiny val the method reaches Success 0.637, SPL 0.313 and DTS 1.568 m versus SemExp's 0.579, 0.280 and 2.050 m, a 10-12% relative gain. Averaged over five training splits, Success is 0.629.
limitations: Small-scale evaluation (10 training scenes, 5 val scenes, 6 categories) and only SemExp as a real baseline
No ablations of the encoder, actor-critic or Q-regularization; the sources of the gain are not isolated
